How to Evaluate a Titanium Dioxide Grade

01

Define the application

Record the resin or material system, end use, processing conditions and performance targets that the grade must be evaluated against.

02

Confirm whether process matters

Identify whether chloride or sulfate production-process classification is a required sourcing parameter. Process classification does not determine application suitability.

03

Review applicable technical data

Review information issued for the grade you are evaluating. Do not infer missing values from another grade, an older source or an unrelated TDS.

04

Identify destination and document needs

Confirm the destination market and the technical, quality, compliance or origin documents required for the applicable request.

05

Validate in the buyer's system

Confirm final suitability through the buyer's own formulation, processing conditions, performance requirements and qualification process.

Buyer Questions

Can one titanium dioxide grade be used in more than one application?

Yes. Some listed grades have multiple application relationships. Use the listed applications to find relevant product pages, then evaluate the grade against your formulation, processing conditions and required performance.

Which grades are listed in this product center?

The product center lists 14 grades: M-350, M-510, M-896, M-996, M-2196, M-895, M-200, M-108, M-210, M-340, M-886, M-52, M-2377 and CR-901.

What is the difference between application and process selection?

Application selection groups grades by listed use-case relationships, while process selection groups grades by their production-process classification. A process classification does not determine application suitability on its own.

What if no grade is shown for my application?

A missing result means that the selector has no listed grade for that application. It should not automatically be interpreted as a technical rejection of every grade. Buyers can contact the team when a requirement is not represented in the selector.
